remarks_1999: Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Exam. at Amer. Place, March 1946. . . . No signature [note of stretcher inscription]. House with flagpole. See gallery photograph, 9–b. (This is from memory –– did not compare gal. photo. with ptg.)." Stretcher inscription dates 1921 and indicates no. 75 in the 1923 New York (Anderson). Stretcher inscription, Abiquiú Notebooks, Downtown Gallery Archive, Whitney Archive date 1922. Pictured in 1923 New York (Anderson) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 20. Either this or cat. nos. 446 or 481 mentioned in 1934 New York (An American Place) exhibition in *New York Times* (1934). O'Keeffe wrote: "At Lake George there was a small square house that had been the wooden part of the large greenhouse. Two electric wires ran to it from the farmhouse and there was a fine weathervane on top of it. In front of the little house was a tall white flagpole and there were rows of lavender and white lilacs that ran around it. Stieglitz used the little house as a dark room for his photographic work so the door, when open, was always black" (*Georgia O'Keeffe* [1976], unpaginated, text accompanying entry 36). See cat. nos. 446, 481. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.title: Little House

description: A tall, thin white pole rises out of a circular patch of green earth and extends through the composition. Behind the pole stands a white house with a pitched black roof and a red chimney. Dark green trees and a large, deep blue mountain range fill the background. A pink and blue sky dotted with dark blue clouds hangs above.
title: Little House
